mainTopic: The אורכתא (power of attorney) for movable property and the collector's status, followed by a משנה on when a thief pays תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה and the גמרא's question whether it fits רבי עקיבא.
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier argument: רבי יוחנן's rule to follow a סתם משנה does not apply when that משנה reflects only one lone חכם. Then the חכמים of נהרדעא rule that one does not write an אורכתא, a document letting someone else collect for you, for movable property. אמימר explains this with רבי יוחנן's rule that an owner cannot be מקדיש an item that is not in his possession. A second version limits the ruling to property the holder denies having, because the document would look like a lie. The נהרדעי add that an אורכתא must say 'go, sue, win and collect for yourself.' Otherwise the debtor can say 'you are not my opponent.' אביי adds that giving the collector even part of the item is enough. אמימר, רב אשי and a third view argue whether the collector may keep what he collects, and the הלכה is that he is only a שליח. A new משנה then lists cases where a thief still pays תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה, with רבי שמעון exempting two of them. The גמרא asks whether the משנה goes against רבי עקיבא's rule of 'דבר ולא חצי דבר', and it begins a ברייתא as the source for that rule, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's rule does not cover a lone opinion
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of an earlier argument: רבי יוחנן never said to follow an unattributed משנה when it reflects only one individual's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: He did not say his rule about an unattributed משנה for a case where it reflects a single individual.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of the previous discussion. The גמרא is finishing its point that רבי יוחנן's rule 'the הלכה follows a סתם משנה' does not apply when that משנה is only one חכם's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion asked whether the חסידים and רבי דוסא might be the same person. If they were one person, the unattributed משנה would be a lone view, and רבי יוחנן's rule would not apply to it. Since רבי יוחנן himself said the חסידים and רבי דוסא said the same thing, they are two people, so the problem cannot be solved this way.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed ruling, stated with no name attached
A single individual, a lone opinion
He did not say (his rule did not cover this case)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new topic. It is the end of a sentence from the previous discussion, so it only makes sense together with what came before.

phrases.english: regarding an unattributed משנה of a single individual, he did not say [his rule].
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוחנן, who said the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the argument from the previous section of the daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's rule to follow a סתם משנה applies only when it is not the view of a lone individual.

steps.title: No authorization document for movable property
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים of נהרדעא rule that one does not write an אורכתא for movable property.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נהרדעי say: we do not write a power-of-attorney document for movable property.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The חכמים of נהרדעא state a rule: you cannot write a document that lets someone else collect your movable property for you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אורכתא lets an agent go to court and collect on the owner's behalf, for example a loan or a deposit. The נהרדעי say this does not work for מטלטלין. They do not give a reason here, and the next step asks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים of the city of נהרדעא
A document authorizing someone to collect or sue on your behalf (power of attorney)

phrases.english: The Nehardeans say:
We do not write an authorization document for movable property.
phrases.notes: Think of property someone else is holding for you, like a loan or a deposit, that you want an agent to collect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a brand-new topic, unrelated to the previous argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אורכתא is not written for מטלטלין.

steps.title: רב אשי asks for the reason
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks אמימר why the נהרדעי ruled this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a simple question: why can't we write an אורכתא for movable property? This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was stated with no reason, and it is not obvious why movable property should be different. This is a request for an explanation, not an attack on the rule.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason why an אורכתא cannot be written for מטלטלין.

steps.title: The reason comes from רבי יוחנן's rule on stolen items
steps.stepSummary: אמימר explains that the ruling is based on רבי יוחנן's statement that neither the thief nor the owner can be מקדיש a stolen item before the owner gives up hope.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: because of רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן said: if someone stole and the owners have not given up hope, neither of them can be מקדיש the item. The thief cannot, because it is not his. The owner cannot, because it is not in his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers by quoting רבי יוחנן. An owner cannot be מקדיש an item that is not in his possession, even though it still belongs to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אורכתא works by handing the agent rights to the item. Movable property held by someone else is not in the owner's possession, just like the stolen item in רבי יוחנן's case. If the owner cannot be מקדיש it, he also cannot transfer rights in it to an agent, so the document does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: He stole (took by force or openly)
The owner giving up hope of getting the item back
To dedicate an item to the בית המקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a basic idea: owning something is not the same as having it in your control, and both may be needed to transfer it.

phrases.english: He said to him: Because of Rabbi Yochanan,
as Rabbi Yochanan said:
If one stole and the owners did not give up hope,
neither of them can consecrate it;
this one because it is not his,
and that one because it is not in his possession.
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the owner. It still belongs to him, but he does not hold it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's question from step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An owner cannot transfer rights in an item that is not in his possession, as shown by רבי יוחנן's ruling about הקדש of a stolen item. So an אורכתא for מטלטלין held by someone else does not work.
steps.whatToRemember: Version one: no אורכתא for any movable property, because something not in your possession cannot be passed on, just as it cannot be made הקדש.

steps.title: A second version: only property that was denied
steps.stepSummary: Another version of the נהרדעי's ruling: no אורכתא is written for movable property that the holder has denied having.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: the נהרדעי say we do not write an authorization document for movable property that he denied.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the same ruling. Here the ban applies only when the person holding the property denies that he has it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the ban covered all movable property. In this version, it is limited to a case where the holder or borrower denies owing anything. This narrows the rule a lot.

keyTerms.meaning: He denied it (claimed he has nothing of the owner's)

phrases.english: There are those who say: the Nehardeans say:
We do not write an authorization document for movable property that he denied.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person holding the property, like the borrower or the one keeping a deposit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, narrower version of the ruling in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אורכתא is not written for מטלטלין that the holder denies having.

steps.title: Why denial matters, and what follows from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the reason is that the document looks false, so if he did not deny it, we do write the document.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is only because he denied it, since it looks like a lie. But if he did not deny it, we write it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second version. When the holder denies it, the document looks like a lie, so we do not write it. If he did not deny it, we do write it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the holder denies it, it is unclear whether the owner really owns anything, so a document saying 'I give you my property' looks false. The reason here is about how the document looks, not about lacking possession. So according to this version, an אורכתא for movable property that was not denied is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It looks like, it appears as

steps.whatToRemember: Version one: never write an אורכתא for movable property. Version two: only not when the holder denies it, because the document would look like a lie. Otherwise it is written.
steps.confusionAlert: The two versions have different reasons. The first is about the owner lacking possession, from רבי יוחנן. The second is about the document looking false. That is why they give different results.

phrases.english: The reason is that he denied it, since it looks like a lie;
but if he did not deny it, we do write it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for the second version in step 5 and draws a practical result from it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In the second version, the problem is only that the document looks false when the holder denies it. Without a denial, an אורכתא for מטלטלין may be written.

steps.title: An authorization document must say 'collect for yourself'
steps.stepSummary: The נהרדעי rule that an אורכתא without the words 'go, sue, acquire and collect for yourself' has no legal force.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נהרדעי also said: an authorization document that does not say 'Go, take him to court, win, and collect it for yourself' has no substance.
steps.whatsHappening: The נהרדעי give another rule about the אורכתא: it must include the phrase 'collect for yourself,' or it is worthless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps dealt with when we write an אורכתא at all. Now the focus is on its wording. Without the key phrase, the document does not actually work.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים of the city נהרדעא
And take it out for yourself
It has no substance, it is worthless

phrases.english: And the Sages of Neharde'a say:
An authorization document in which it is not written
"Go, sue, win, and collect it for yourself"
has no substance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new rule from the same נהרדעי about the same kind of document.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אורכתא lacking 'go, sue, win and collect for yourself' is invalid.

steps.title: Why: the debtor can say 'you are not my opponent'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason and explains that without that phrase, the debtor can refuse to argue with the collector.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the other side can say to him: you are not the one I have a case with.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the phrase is needed and answers: otherwise the debtor can tell the collector, 'I have no business with you.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the collector is just a messenger, the debtor can insist on facing only the real owner. Writing 'for yourself' makes the collector a real party to the case, so the debtor must answer him.

keyTerms.meaning: The opposing party in a court case

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because that other one can say to him:
phrases.notes: 'That other one' is the person holding the item or owing the money.

phrases.english: You are not my legal opponent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the rule in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the 'for yourself' clause is required.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Without it, the debtor can refuse to litigate with someone who is not his בעל דברים.

steps.title: Giving even part of the item is enough
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that if the document gives the collector only a half, third, or quarter, it still works for the whole item.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: if it says half, a third, or a quarter, then since the debtor must go to court with him over part, he must go to court with him over all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds that the owner does not have to give the collector the whole item; giving him a share is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the collector owns a share, the debtor must face him in court for that share. Since the case is already being argued with him, it is argued with him for the whole item.

keyTerms.meaning: Since (one thing is true, so is the other)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
And if it is written in it
for a half, for a third, or for a quarter,
phrases.notes: He means the owner gave the collector only that share of the item.

phrases.english: since he must argue the case over half,
he must argue the case over all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule: a partial transfer also satisfies the requirement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Transferring a half, third, or quarter is enough, because the case then proceeds with the collector for the whole item.

steps.title: אמימר: the collector may keep what he seizes
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that if the collector grabs the item for himself, the court does not take it from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: if he seized it, we do not take it away from him.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר rules on a case where the collector keeps the collected item for himself: the court does not take it away from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the document says 'collect for yourself,' אמימר treats the wording as a real transfer to the collector. So he may hold on to what he took.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not take it away from him

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
If he seized it, we do not take it away from him.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the collector who holds the אורכתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical result from the 'for yourself' wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A collector who seizes the collected item keeps it.

steps.title: רב אשי: the collector is only an agent
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees: since the owner wrote 'I take responsibility for whatever comes out of the case,' he made the collector a שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: since he wrote to him, 'Whatever results from the case, I accept upon myself,' he made him an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues with אמימר, pointing to another line in the document that shows the collector is only a messenger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner takes on the costs and results of the lawsuit himself. That shows the case really belongs to the owner, so the collector is a שליח and cannot keep the item.
steps.confusionAlert: Both phrases are in the same document. 'Collect for yourself' is only there so the debtor must answer him; the 'I accept' line shows he is really a שליח.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Since he wrote to him
"Whatever results from the case, I accept upon myself"
he made him an agent.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר כֵּיוָן דְּכַתְבֵיהּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with אמימר's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The collector is a שליח and may not keep the item.

steps.title: Another opinion: the collector is a partner
steps.stepSummary: A different version says the owner made the collector a שותף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: he made him a partner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third view: the collector is neither full owner nor only an agent, but a partner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a middle position between אמימר and רב אשי. The collector owns part of the item along with the owner.

phrases.english: And there is one who says:
He made him a partner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different view from רב אשי's 'agent' position.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The collector is a שותף in the item.

steps.title: The difference: may he take half?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what difference agent versus partner makes, and answers: whether he may seize half.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the practical difference? Whether he may seize half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the 'agent' and 'partner' views differ in practice, and answers that it is about taking half the item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A partner owns half, so he may grab half for himself. An agent owns nothing, so he may grab nothing.

phrases.english: What is the practical difference?
To seize half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the practical gap between steps 11 and 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical difference between שליח and שותף.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שותף may seize half; a שליח may not.

steps.title: The ruling: he is an agent
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows the view that the collector is a שליח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: he made him an agent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: the collector is only a שליח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sides with רב אשי against אמימר and against the partner view. So the collector may not keep any part of what he collects.
steps.whatToRemember: An אורכתא must say 'collect for yourself' so the debtor must answer the collector, but in the end the collector is only a שליח and must hand everything over to the owner.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: he made him an agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the views in steps 10 through 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The collector is a שליח and may not seize any of the collected item for himself.

steps.title: Theft and slaughter proven by the same or different witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens: if the theft was proven by two עדים, and the slaughter or sale was proven by those same עדים or by two other עדים, the thief pays תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone stole an animal, as two witnesses testified, and then slaughtered or sold it, as those same witnesses testified or as two other witnesses testified, he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with its first case. The theft and the slaughter or sale can be proven by one set of עדים or by two separate sets, and the thief pays the fine either way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fine has two parts: stealing, then slaughtering or selling. The משנה teaches that one pair of עדים does not have to prove both parts. Each part can be proven by its own pair, and the full fine still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (a new משנה starts here)
Based on the testimony of two witnesses
The fourfold (sheep) or fivefold (ox) payment a thief owes

phrases.english: MISHNA: He stole, based on two [witnesses],
and slaughtered or sold, based on them,
or based on two other [witnesses] —
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ended with the הלכה that the collector is a שליח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The theft and the slaughter or sale can be proven by separate pairs of עדים, and the thief still pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.title: Selling or slaughtering while committing a sin
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists three cases: selling on שבת, selling for עבודה זרה, and slaughtering on יום הכיפורים. The ruling that he still pays comes at the end of the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stole and sold on שבת; if he stole and sold for idol worship; if he stole and slaughtered on יום הכיפורים...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three cases where the sale or slaughter itself was a sin. This line is a list and does not finish the sentence; the ruling (he pays) comes at the end of the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the act that triggers the fine (selling or slaughtering) was done in a forbidden way. You might think that sin cancels the payment. The משנה says he still pays, and the גמרא will later explore why.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these cases have no ruling. The words 'he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment' at the end of the next line cover these cases too.

phrases.english: He stole and sold on Shabbat;
he stole and sold for idol worship;
he stole and slaughtered on Yom Kippur;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more cases to the משנה's list, this time where the sale or slaughter involved a sin.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling on שבת, selling for עבודה זרה, or slaughtering on יום הכיפורים still leads to the fourfold or fivefold payment (the ruling is stated in the next line).

steps.title: Stealing from one's father, or consecrating after slaughter
steps.stepSummary: If he stole from his father, slaughtered or sold the animal, and then his father died, or if he stole, slaughtered, and then made the animal הקדש, he still pays תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה. This ruling also covers the cases in the previous line.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stole from his father's property, slaughtered or sold it, and afterward his father died; or if he stole and slaughtered and afterward consecrated it, he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two cases where something happened after the slaughter or sale: the father died, or the thief made the animal הקדש. It then states the ruling: he pays, and this ruling covers the שבת, עבודה זרה and יום הכיפורים cases too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the father dies, the thief may inherit the animal, so it seems he is now paying himself. With הקדש, the animal now belongs to the Temple. The משנה teaches that the fine was already set when he slaughtered or sold, so what happens later does not cancel it.

keyTerms.meaning: He consecrated it (made it Temple property)

phrases.english: He stole from his father's [property] and slaughtered or sold [it],
and afterward his father died;
he stole and slaughtered, and afterward consecrated [it] —
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds cases where something happened after the slaughter or sale, and closes the sentence the previous line began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Events after the slaughter or sale, such as the father's death or making the animal הקדש, do not cancel the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.title: A useless or forbidden slaughter still counts
steps.stepSummary: Slaughtering for medicine or for dogs, a שחיטה that turns out to be טריפה, and slaughtering חולין in the עזרה all still obligate תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he stole and slaughtered for medicine or for dogs; or slaughtered and it was found to be טריפה; or slaughtered a non-sacred animal in the Temple courtyard, he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends its list with cases where the slaughter was not done for eating, did not make the meat permitted, or was itself forbidden. The thief still pays the fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case the שחיטה was not a normal, kosher slaughter for eating: it was for medicine or dogs, the animal was טריפה, or it was חולין slaughtered in the עזרה, which is forbidden. The משנה teaches that it still counts as slaughter for the fine.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten

steps.whatToRemember: Throughout this משנה, odd circumstances do not cancel the fine: separate witnesses, a sin during the act, later ownership or הקדש, or a useless or forbidden שחיטה. Every case ends with 'he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.'

phrases.english: He stole and slaughtered for medicine or for dogs;
one who slaughters and it was found [to be] a tereifa;
one who slaughters non-sacred animals in the Temple courtyard —
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's list with cases where the slaughter itself was useless or forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slaughter that is useless for eating or forbidden still counts, and the thief pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.title: רבי שמעון exempts the thief in the last two cases
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees with the משנה about the last two cases: a שחיטה that turned out to be טריפה, and slaughtering חולין in the עזרה. He says the thief does not pay תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון exempts the thief in these two cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a dissenting opinion. רבי שמעון says that in the last two cases from the list, the thief does not pay the extra fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are a שחיטה that made the animal טריפה, and חולין slaughtered in the עזרה. In both, the slaughter does not do its normal job of making the meat permitted to eat. רבי שמעון's view is that a שחיטה like that does not count as a שחיטה, so the 'slaughter' needed for the fine never really happened. The other cases on the list, such as slaughter for medicine or for dogs, are a normal kosher slaughter, so he agrees the thief pays there.

keyTerms.meaning: In these two: the last two cases of the list
A slaughter that does not make the meat permitted. רבי שמעון holds it is not considered a שחיטה.

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא קמא says every case on the list obligates תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה. רבי שמעון exempts only the טריפה case and the חולין in the עזרה case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon exempts
in these two.
phrases.notes: These are the last two cases from Step 18: the slaughter that turned out טריפה, and חולין slaughtered in the עזרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling of Step 18 for two of its cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון: no תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה when the שחיטה was טריפה or was חולין in the עזרה.

steps.title: Is the משנה against רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא says that עדים must testify to a whole matter ('דבר'), not to half of one.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא? Because if it followed רבי עקיבא, there is a problem: he says the word 'matter' means a whole matter, and not half a matter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking whose opinion the משנה follows. It suggests that the משנה cannot match רבי עקיבא's rule about testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Look back at the opening case of the משנה (Step 15). One pair of עדים saw the theft, and a different pair saw the slaughter or sale. The slaughter alone makes the thief owe nothing. It only matters together with the theft, so the second pair is testifying to just 'half a matter'. רבי עקיבא learns from the word 'דבר' in the פסוק that such half-testimony does not count, so by his view the thief should not pay the fine.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
Shall we say? It introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test.
But he said! It points to a known statement that causes a problem.
A whole matter, not half a matter. Testimony must establish a complete case on its own.

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'half a matter' does not mean the עדים only saw part of the event. It means their testimony, taken alone, does not create any legal result.
steps.whyThisMatters: If the משנה really goes against רבי עקיבא, that is a big claim, so the גמרא will check whether the משנה can still fit his view.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Shall we say that our mishna
is not in line with Rabbi Akiva?
For if it were Rabbi Akiva,
didn't he say: "a matter":
phrases.notes: From דברים 19:15, 'by two or three witnesses a matter shall be established.'

phrases.english: and not half a matter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא's analysis by returning to the opening case of the משנה (Step 15).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משנה's ruling about separate pairs of עדים contradict רבי עקיבא's rule of 'דבר ולא חצי דבר'?
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a second pair of עדים testifying only to the slaughter or sale still makes the thief pay תשלומי ארבעה וחמשה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבי עקיבא, testimony to half a matter does not count. The slaughter-עדים testify to half a matter, so the fine should not apply.

steps.title: A ברייתא begins: the source for רבי עקיבא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא as the source for רבי עקיבא's rule. In it, רבי יוסי tells about a meeting between his father אבא חלפתא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי. The ברייתא continues past this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי said: When my father חלפתא went to רבי יוחנן בן נורי to learn תורה (and some say: when רבי יוחנן בן נורי went to my father...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its proof that רבי עקיבא really holds 'דבר ולא חצי דבר'. It starts telling a story, and the story continues right after this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is not quoted here as a new topic. It is the source for the statement of רבי עקיבא used in Step 20. רבי יוסי tells the story about his father, and there are two versions of who went to learn from whom. That detail does not change the point the story will make.

keyTerms.meaning: Father חלפתא, the father of רבי יוסי

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei said:
When father Ḥalafta went
phrases.notes: 'אבא' here is רבי יוסי talking about his own father.

phrases.english: to Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri
to learn Torah,
and some say:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אֵצֶל אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri went to father

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the רבי עקיבא statement cited in Step 20.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא holds testimony must cover a whole matter, not half a matter.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יוסי telling about אבא חלפתא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי (the story continues in the next section).
